stories.title: Meghan Markle's estranged father arrested for child pornography possession: US authorities
summary: Thomas Markle, father of Prince Harry’s wife Meghan Markle, has been arrested for possessing child pornography, the US Justice Department said on Friday.
Authorities in the Philippines, where Markle had previously lived for some time, began investigating him last month over the allegations.

British tabloid The Sun reported last month that Markle’s son, Thomas Markle Jr, had discovered the child sex abuse images while going through boxes found in his father’s former home in the Philippines.

stories.title: Bilawal urges federal govt to engage all political forces instead of ‘fighting everyone’
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday urged the PML-N-led federal government to engage all political and social stakeholders rather than “fighting everyone”.
Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

stories.title: Elon Musk's futuristic Cybertruck rolls toward exit
summary: Tesla fans lamented the departure of the Cybertruck on X, the social media platform Musk owns, but the tycoon reassured them that the Cybertruck fleet “will be around for a long time”.
As US demand slumped, Tesla began selling the truck abroad, starting deliveries in South Korea in November 2025 and in the United Arab Emirates in January.
Tesla began production at the Texas plant in April and started offering paid Cybercab rides in Austin in September through its existing Robotaxi service.

stories.title: Turkish vessel to arrive in Karachi between Nov 17-20 to begin offshore oil, gas exploration
summary: ISLAMABAD: A Turkish seismic vessel will arrive in Karachi between November 17 and 20 to begin offshore oil and gas exploration, the Petroleum Division said on Friday.

The announcement followed a meeting between Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and relevant agencies to review preparations and arrangements for the arrival of the seismic vessel of Turkish Petroleum Offshore Company (TPOC) in Pakistan.

The meeting reviewed operational, logistical, maritime, security and interdepartmental arrangements for the vessel’s arrival and commencement of the offshore exploration campaign to build Pakistan’s energy security.

stories.title: Usman Khan’s unbeaten century powers Pakistan to emphatic win over UAE in U-19 Asia Cup
summary: Usman led the charge with an unbeaten 139 off 120 balls, hitting 21 fours and a six.
Qadir remained unbeaten on 20 off 19 deliveries, striking a four and a six.
UAE managed 224 in their allotted 50 overs, with Noorullah Ayobi leading the scoring with a brisk 70 off 55 balls, including three fours and six sixes.

stories.title: EU charges TikTok over harmful algorithmic 'rabbit hole' effects, tells it to change 'For You' feed
summary: It said the platform should change the design of its ‘For You’ feed algorithm and should rely more on users’ explicit preferences, increase the accessibility and usability of user controls and regularly test its algorithm, among other changes.
Even when users tell TikTok they do not like certain content, the platform’s algorithm continues to suggest similar videos.
In its preliminary findings, the EU said TikTok did not “adequately assess” how its recommendation algorithm put users’ wellbeing at risk.

stories.title: How China's clean-tech machine is reshaping the global climate fight
summary: The $132bn figure derived by Reuters for China’s global climate contribution also includes an estimated $40 billion of Chinese foreign direct investment into clean-technology projects in developing countries.

That brings China’s contribution to nearly equal to the $137bn in climate finance that wealthy nations provided to poorer ones in 2024 under their UN climate pledges, according to the most recent figures provided by the OECD.
Nearly two thirds of China’s exports of solar panels, and the cells needed to make them, went to the developing world last year, according to Reuters analysis of customs data.

stories.title: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO
summary: Mahmood was appointed on Sep 23 as the first secretary general of the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

The Makkah Defence Alliance has garnered particular attention as Saudi Arabia faces attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, including a deadly strike that closed Riyadh’s international airport for two weeks last month.

Pakistan, others actively making efforts for peace in Middle East In his briefing, Khan also touched upon the crisis in the Gulf, saying that Pakistan would continue its efforts to facilitate dialogue in the conflict involving Iran and the United States.

stories.title: Imaan, Hadi move IHC against conviction in security breach case
summary: ISLAMABAD: Human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse Hadi Ali Chattha on Friday filed appeals in the Islamabad High Court (IHC) against their convictions by an anti-terrorism court in the security breach case.

It further contended that state counsel was imposed on the appellants against their stated wishes and that the trial court proceeded with the case despite a transfer application pending before the high court, in violation of Section 526(8) of the CrPC.

The organisations called for the convictions to be seen in the context of “successive, politically motivated, criminal proceedings” against the couple, which were “solely to punish them for and deter them from continuing their peaceful, permissible human rights work”.

stories.title: PM seeks roadmap for ‘100pc’ digital payments system, stresses countrywide internet access
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday directed authorities to prepare a “clear roadmap and time-bound targets” for establishing a 100 per cent digital payments system in the country.
The directives came during a high-level meeting he chaired in Islamabad regarding the promotion of a cashless economy in the country, according to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The premier directed the relevant officials to present a “clear roadmap and time-bound targets for establishing a 100pc digital payments system in the country”. “The issues faced by users in the digital payments system should be resolved immediately,” PM Shehbaz said.

stories.title: Pakistan, UK agree to expand cooperation on counterterrorism, narcotics
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and the United Kingdom on Friday agreed to enhance cooperation in the areas of counterterrorism, anti-narcotics, cybercrime and immigration, according to the interior ministry.
The understanding was reached during delegation-level talks between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and visiting British Minister of State for Security Dan Jarvis at the Ministry of Interior.
Naqvi told the British minister that Pakistan had foiled 330 cases involving narcotics smuggling to the UK over the past few years.

stories.title: Global tech stocks suffer bloodbath as US midterms fuel AI fears
summary: The London, Paris and Frankfurt stock markets shed around 2pc nearing the halfway stage despite featuring few technology firms.

Can AI bull markets elsewhere hold up on their own?” Tokyo dived 6pc on Friday as Japanese tech investor SoftBank gave back more than 10pc, while chipmaker Kioxia collapsed 8.7pc and semiconductor tester Advantest retreated 5pc.

The selling indicates investors are starting to factor in increased local opposition to data centres, with analysts saying markets have yet to fully consider the cost such building has imposed on communities.

stories.title: Human bondage
summary: The recent praise for Pakistan from the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights for raising the minimum marriageable age to 18 is, no doubt, welcome.
The Constitution outlaws all forced labour and slavery; the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1992, criminalises the practice.
Yet, the failure to enforce the law and insufficient efforts to bridge the distance between constitutional rights and their fulfilment have forced poor people into a life of bondage.

stories.title: Israeli opposition leader warns of deepening crisis with US amid planned military aid cuts
summary: Responding to criticism, Netanyahu's office said US military aid to Israel had historically enjoyed bipartisan support and portrayed the planned shift as a transition “from aid to partnership”.
Eisenkot receives backing from 67 lawmakers The remarks came after President Isaac Herzog concluded consultations on Thursday with parties elected to the Knesset.
Herzog said factions representing 67 of the 120 lawmakers had recommended Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, while parties representing 46 lawmakers backed Netanyahu.

stories.title: Democrats planning flood of AI bills when they take control of Congress
summary: Democrats are planning to unleash a flood of new legislation targeting artificial intelligence systems and data-centre development when they take control of the US Congress in January, lawmakers, congressional aides and advocates said.

Democrats plan on introducing bills aimed at shielding consumers from rising electricity costs tied to data centres, requiring independent testing of advanced AI systems and clarifying when AI companies can be held liable for harm caused by their products, they said.

Most US voters think ​Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new ​regulations for the technology, ⁠according to a Reuters poll published in October.

stories.title: Sperm whale spotted off Sindh's coast for first time: WWF-Pakistan
summary: A sperm whale has been sighted off the Sindh coast for the first time, around 40 nautical miles southwest of Karachi, the World Wide Fund for Nature-Pakistan (WWF-Pakistan) said on Friday.
According to WWF-Pakistan, 26 cetacean species, including whales and dolphins, have been documented in the country’s waters.
The organisation said its research and monitoring efforts had also helped document several toothed whale species in Pakistan’s waters for the first time.

stories.title: Eight killed, 30 injured in bus-truck collision on Hazara Motorway
summary: ABBOTTABAD: At least eight people were killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a dumper truck near the Havelian Interchange on the Hazara Motorway early Friday morning, rescue officials said.
A day earlier, a collision between a passenger bus and truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Pakpattan.
Last week, at least five people were killed and 27 others injured when a passenger bus plunged into a drain in Punjab’s Hafizabad district.

stories.title: Trump declares full support for ‘super intelligence’
summary: He had previously signalled his administration’s hardline stance on the terminology, saying the White House considers those who continue using the term “artificial intelligence” rather than “super intelligence” an “enemy”.
The administration has also established a Super Intelligence Force to coordinate the federal government’s approach to the technology.

stories.title: Meta pauses planned terms updates, keeps existing rules in place
summary: Meta has paused planned ​updates to its ‌Commercial Terms, Product Catalog Terms, Self-Serve ​Ad Terms ​and Ad Creative Generative ⁠AI Terms, ​meaning the changes will ​not take effect on November 20, 2026, ​the company ​said on Friday.

"We're pausing the ‌changes ⁠as we continue to engage with stakeholders and ​take ​our ⁠time to get this right. ​In the ​meantime, ⁠our existing terms remain in ⁠effect," ​a spokesperson ​said in a statement to to Harvard’s Nieman Lab.
However, the brief delay failed to ease customer concerns, prompting Meta to announce on Facebook’s Business Help Centre that the update had been paused indefinitely.

stories.title: Apple's predictive text restrictions include 'Dictator Trump' and 'Sleepy Joe,' researcher finds
summary: Apple has an undisclosed multilingual gray list of tens of thousands of words and phrases that its iOS keyboard will not autocomplete or swipe-type, a researcher said on Friday.

But other phrases are ​just politically salient, like "dictator Trump" and "sleepy Joe." In an email, Apple did not comment directly on Kauffman's findings, including the size or composition of its list, or its reasons for flagging certain political terms.
It said ​that iPhone users always had the option to type specific words or phrases and could always override any predictive text suggestions.

stories.title: Turkish seismic vessel to reach Karachi in mid Nov for offshore oil, gas exploration
summary: A Turkish seismic research vessel is expected to arrive in Karachi between November 17 and 20 to begin offshore oil and gas exploration, the Petroleum Division said on Friday, marking Pakistan's first major push to revive offshore exploration activities in two decades.

Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik chaired a high-level meeting in Islamabad to review arrangements for the arrival of the Turkish Petroleum Corporation's (TPAO) seismic vessel, according to a statement issued by the division.

Also Read: Turkish Petroleum to soon begin offshore drilling in Pakistan: petroleum minister Separately, Turkish Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar confirmed that the country's seismic research vessel Oruç Reis was heading towards waters off Pakistan.

stories.title: Indian Christians warn of attacks in West Bengal
summary: Indian Christian leaders say they suffered systematic attacks on their faith after a spate of church vandalism and assaults in West Bengal state, they told AFP on Friday.
Christians account for less than one per cent of West Bengal’s population, according to the last national census.

The Washington-based India Hate Lab research group said in a September report that it had documented 60 incidents targeting Christians in West Bengal after the BJP took power, including assaults, vandalism and raids on prayer meetings.

stories.title: Two policemen held in ‘gang rape’ case in Swat
summary: SWAT: The Rahimabad police on Thursday arrested two suspects, both serving police constables, in connection with the alleged gang rape of a woman who had travelled to Swat from Peshawar.
Taking immediate notice of the complaint, Swat DPO Umar Khan directed police to arrest the suspects.
When contacted, DPO Swat Umar Khan confirmed that both suspects were serving police constables.

stories.title: Hegseth vows to keep fighting from Pentagon, defends Iran war
summary: Trump also praised Hegseth's role in US military operations in Venezuela and Iran.
One Trump adviser said Hegseth "could be on the chopping block" because of the Iran war.

"Regardless of how ⁠people feel about the war, which I believe is a courageous and historic effort that will ensure Iran never gets nuclear weapons, we need to continue, as President Trump did in his first term, to rebuild our military," Hegseth said.

stories.title: Asif sees attempt to set ground for 'alternative arrangement' in Punjab amid Maryam-Salik row
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has claimed that Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s recent corruption allegations against the Punjab government are part of efforts to set the ground for an “alternative arrangement”.
He alleged during the ARY News’ programme that Salik’s allegations “are part of setting the stage for some post-period”. “This statement was given selectively against Punjab.
Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab.

stories.title: Gohar demands immediate implementation of SC order on Imran's medical treatment
summary: Also Read: PTI seeks Imran's immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital over renewed blood pressure concerns The remarks came amid renewed concerns within the PTI over Imran's health.
She further said the Supreme Court's order requiring Imran's immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment had not been implemented.
Akram called for the immediate implementation of the August 18 order and demanded that Imran be transferred to Shifa International Hospital for treatment by his personal and family-appointed doctors.

stories.title: Wall Street critic Elizabeth Warren could be at the height of her power in new Congress
summary: Democratic progressive and one-time presidential candidate Elizabeth Warren has long been a vocal ​Wall Street critic, but next year the US senator from Massachusetts will likely have more power over the industry than ever before.

Elizabeth will likely probe the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's August decision to approve a bank charter ​for President Donald Trump-backed World Liberty Financial, said one person familiar with her thinking.
"I'm ready to team up with any Republican who is listening to the American people," Elizabeth wrote in a Thursday opinion piece in Time magazine ​on Senate Democrats' priorities.

stories.title: Bilawal urges political parties to set aside differences, focus on economic crisis
summary: Bilawal chaired a high-level meeting at Bhutto House in Naudero, which was attended by Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, Chief Secretary Asif Haider Shah and members of parliament and senior government officials.
Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman @BBhuttoZardari presides over a high-level meeting today on key development projects in Larkana Division at Bhutto House, Naudero.
Secretary Public Health Engineering Sohail Qureshi informed the meeting that a feasibility study had been completed for a project covering water supply, sewerage and rainwater drainage in Larkana.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia denies WSJ report claiming Houthis demanded $51bn to halt hostilities
summary: Saudi Arabia has denied a report by the US-based Wall Street Journal (WSJ) that Yemen’s Houthis had demanded $51 billion from kingdom in return for a “negotiated halt” to the ongoing hostilities between the two sides.
The WSJ report and the Saudi denial has come amid renewed hostilities between Riyadh and the Houthis, linked to the larger Middle East conflict.
Then in July, the Houthis triggered a return to hostilities in Yemen when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.

stories.title: PM directs authorities to map out cashless economy transition
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday directed the relevant authorities to prepare a clear roadmap, with specific timelines and targets, for establishing a fully digital payment system across the country as the government steps up efforts to promote a cashless economy.

Chairing a high-level meeting in Islamabad to review progress on the government's cashless economy initiative, the prime minister said promoting digital payments was among the government's top priorities, adding that positive results had started to emerge.
"From November 16, all payments into Asaan Assignment Accounts across the country would be made through the Raast digital payment system," the statement said.

stories.title: Newsroom bomb threats follow escalating European flight hoaxes
summary: Offices of Irish media groups evacuated due to bomb threats The offices of Irish media groups including national broadcaster RTE were evacuated ​following bomb threats on Friday that a presenter on ‌one of the impacted radio stations, Newstalk, said had been deemed a hoax.

The presenter of RTE Radio One's mid ​morning news show said he understood that the email was purported to be ‌from ⁠the same people behind hoax bomb threats that disrupted dozens of passenger flights across Europe on Thursday.

On ​Thursday, an airport source in Italy said bomb threats had been sent to several airlines and ​airport operators in Rome and Milan claiming to be from "fighters of the Male State", a far-right anti-feminist movement banned in Russia.

stories.title: Democrats expand US House majority to 253 seats as midterm vote count continues
summary: Democrats flip Republican-held House seats In New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District, Democrat Zack Mullock defeated Republican incumbent Jeff Van Drew, securing 50.8% of the vote against 48.2%, with 97% of ballots counted.
Democrat Kristina Knickerbocker also defeated Republican incumbent Mike Turner in Ohio's 10th District, winning 49.3% of the vote against 47.7%.

Jessica Killin defeated Republican incumbent Jeff Crank in Colorado's 5th District with 50.5% of the vote, while JoAnna Mendoza unseated Republican incumbent Juan Ciscomani in Arizona's 6th District with 52.8%, according to results with 89% of ballots counted.

stories.title: LIV Golf league to shut down after five years
summary: In a statement, LIV Golf said only that attempts to implement its Restructuring Support Agreement with BC Partners had foundered.
BC Partners Credit said in a statement that there was "great support" for a revamped LIV circuit, but that ultimately no agreement on terms could be reached.
"BC Partners supported a transaction that aligned the interests of players and investors, offering a credible path toward building a sustainable future for LIV Golf," the company said.

stories.title: Britney Spears' 2001 album returns with bonus tracks for 25th anniversary
summary: A special edition of American pop star Britney Spears' third studio album, Britney, was released Friday to mark its 25th anniversary, featuring five previously unreleased songs.

The 23-track collection, released by Legacy Recordings and credited to RCA Records, includes songs from the original 2001 album alongside additional recordings and two remixes, according to its listing on Apple Music.
The 44-year-old singer has not released a full album of new material since Glory in 2016.

stories.title: Martine Rose appointed Balenciaga creative director as Kering seeks fresh ideas
summary: British designer Martine Rose is taking over as creative director at Balenciaga, parent Kering said on Friday, replacing Pierpaolo Piccioli after only 16 months in the role.
Rose, 45, is a menswear designer who founded her eponymous label in London in 2007 and later worked at Balenciaga for three years under then creative director Demna, who now leads Gucci.
Kering has yet to announce a new creative director at Saint Laurent, its second-biggest brand, to replace Anthony Vaccarello who resigned in October after a decade leading the Parisian fashion label.

stories.title: Turkish parliament approves Makkah defence pact with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
summary: The Turkish parliament on Thursday approved a bill ratifying the Makkah Agreement on Joint Defence with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, paving the way for the trilateral security pact to come into force.

The measure, formally titled the Bill on the Approval of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between the Republic of Turkiye, Pakistan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, passed after a lengthy debate among parties.

Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on Aug 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

stories.title: Film 'One in a Million' follows young Syrian refugee's journey over 10 years
summary: Israa was 11 years old and selling cigarettes with her father on a street corner in Turkiye when filmmakers Jack MacInnes and Itab Azzam met the Syrian refugee in 2015.
The intimate coming-of-age story shows Israa and her family crossing borders and adapting in Germany, where new-found freedoms jar with old traditions.
"It was so emotional for us to see this girl... who we'd met 11 years previously ... selling cigarettes on a street corner, being beaten up by police, no one gave a damn about her.

stories.title: Maliha Ali takes bronze at MMA worlds as Pakistan appeals semi-final decision
summary: When Omar Ahmed, president of the Pakistan MMA Federation, asked if she could compete, her response was simple. “Sir, we fight from the heart,” she said. “These hands and feet are just not that important.” That courage carried her to the semi-final.

Maliha’s run at the IMMAF World Championships in Tbilisi, Georgia, ended in a bronze medal and a dispute on Thursday, with the Pakistan MMA Federation filing a formal appeal over her split-decision loss to Russia’s Polina Baldina in the featherweight (65.8kg) semi-final.
Baldina, 23, is a former world champion in a different MMA federation, having won a world title in Khanty-Mansiysk in 2024, and had won three bouts en route to the final.

stories.title: London police chief expects 'many more' complaints against Russell Brand
summary: The chief of London's Metropolitan Police said Friday "many more" women might come forward with accusations against Russell Brand, after the disgraced comedian was convicted of rape and sexual assault.

Brand, 51, was on Thursday found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults against four women following a high-profile trial, in which he was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault against two other women.

'Culture and failings' Once one of the country's most high-profile entertainers, Brand had a reputation for lewd humour and promiscuity, passing through major media organisations including the BBC, Channel 4 and MTV.

stories.title: President Zardari pays tribute on Jammu Martyrs' Day, reaffirms support for Kashmiris
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday paid tribute to the innocent Kashmiri Muslims massacred in Jammu in November 1947.

1/2 Message from President Asif Ali Zardari on Jammu Martyrs’ Day (Youm-e-Shuhada-e-Jammu), 6 November 2026 On Jammu Martyrs’ Day, we solemnly remember and pay tribute to the innocent Kashmiri Muslims massacred in Jammu in November 1947.
Reaffirming Pakistan's principled position on Jammu and Kashmir, President Zardari said the country remained steadfast in its support for the Kashmiri people.
